title: Unstrained C–C cleavage at a chosen bond
open: Cleave and replace a selected unstrained C–C bond in a multifunctional molecule without relying on ring-strain release, privileged directing groups or destructive fragmentation elsewhere.
status: A longstanding skeletal-editing challenge. Alkyne-bridged palladium chemistry in 2025 enabled cleavage in unstrained ketones, esters and amides; arbitrary backbone bonds remain substantially less accessible.
why: Allows molecular frameworks to be diversified after their construction.
key_works: Ding et al. (2025), *Modular esterification of unstrained carbonyls through palladium-catalyzed alkyne bridging C-C bond activation*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-64279-0](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-64279-0).

title: Independent selection of aromatic rings for saturation
open: Hydrogenate a chosen ring in a molecule containing several electronically similar arenes, with independent control of ring selection and stereochemistry while retaining other reducible groups.
status: Longstanding. Directed ruthenium saturation reported in 2025 selects the arene adjacent to a directing moiety, including complex substrates and gram-scale examples; freely selecting other rings remains open.
why: Provides three-dimensional drug analogues without rebuilding the molecule.
key_works: Yu, Yiu, Zhang and Dong (2025), *Site-selective Ru-catalysed saturation of unactivated arenes via directed 6π activation*, [DOI:10.1038/s41929-025-01404-8](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41929-025-01404-8).

title: Position-programmable carbon-to-nitrogen ring editing
open: Replace a selected ring carbon with nitrogen in densely substituted arenes or heteroarenes while preserving the remaining substitution pattern. Independently choose between competing replacement positions using practical reagents.
status: Rapidly developing since the early 2020s. Pyridine-to-pyridazine conversion was demonstrated in 2025 through azide introduction and photochemical rearrangement; general positional editing remains open.
why: Makes medicinal scaffold changes possible late in a synthesis.
key_works: Puriņš, Nakahara and Levin (2025), *Bridging the pyridine-pyridazine synthesis gap by skeletal editing*, [DOI:10.1126/science.adx4762](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adx4762).

title: Carbon isotope exchange at arbitrary skeletal positions
open: Exchange a chosen skeletal carbon for an isotope-labeled carbon in an intact complex molecule without reconstructing its skeleton, losing stereochemical information or extensively scrambling the label.
status: Direct exchange has advanced for selected functional groups. Vanadium-mediated exchange of terminal alkenes was demonstrated in 2025; buried saturated carbons and arbitrary position selection remain open.
why: Simplifies tracer preparation and quantitative studies of molecular fate.
key_works: Krivovicheva et al. (2025), *Vanadium-Mediated Carbon Isotope Exchange of Terminal Alkenes*, [DOI:10.1021/jacs.5c05880](https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.5c05880).

title: Addressable epimerization of every sugar stereocenter
open: Invert a selected stereocenter of an unprotected sugar or chosen oligosaccharide residue while preserving all other centers and glycosidic linkages.
status: Selective rare-sugar epimerizations were demonstrated in 2020; 2026 kinetic-network control extended selected transformations, including GlcNAc-to-GalNAc. Independent access to every position in complex glycans remains unresolved.
why: Converts abundant sugars into otherwise costly stereochemical building blocks.
key_works: Wang, Carder and Wendlandt (2020), *Synthesis of rare sugar isomers through site-selective epimerization*, [DOI:10.1038/s41586-020-1937-1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-020-1937-1).

title: Stereodivergent synthesis of distant acyclic stereocenters
open: Access every configuration of several independently positioned, nonadjacent acyclic stereocenters from the same starting-material set without redesigning the route for each isomer.
status: A multidecade objective. Nickel chain-walking chemistry reported online in 2025 accesses all four stereoisomers for selected 1,3- and 1,4-related centers; longer distances and more centers remain open.
why: Separates stereochemical effects from scaffold effects during drug discovery.
key_works: Ju et al. (2025/2026), *Stereodivergent construction of non-adjacent stereocentres via migratory functionalization of alkenes*, [DOI:10.1038/s41557-025-01994-7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41557-025-01994-7).

title: General mild catalytic amidation without coupling reagents
open: Condense diverse unactivated acids and amines catalytically under mild, concentrated conditions, including hindered and unprotected substrates, with negligible racemization and no stoichiometric activator.
status: Decades old. Phosphorus/catechol catalysis reported in 2025 adds a direct-amidation platform; jointly achieving broad scope, water tolerance, low temperature and catalyst recovery remains open.
why: Removes major reagent and purification burdens from pharmaceutical synthesis.
key_works: Nagano et al. (2025), *Study on Phosphorus Compound/Catechol-Catalyzed Dehydrative Amidation and Its Database Development for Machine Learning*, [DOI:10.1002/chem.202500955](https://doi.org/10.1002/chem.202500955).

title: Main-group carbonylation with complete catalytic turnover
open: Build main-group carbonylation cycles that repeatedly insert CO, selectively transfer the resulting acyl group and regenerate the catalyst without stoichiometric metal consumption.
status: Reversible main-group CO insertion and extrusion remain sparsely developed. Bismuth compounds enabled reversible visible-light-driven steps in 2025; broadly useful complete synthesis cycles remain open.
why: Provides new catalyst architectures for carbonyl-containing chemicals.
key_works: Geist et al. (2025), *Diaryl Bismuthides and Acyl Bismuthanes Enable Visible-Light-Induced Reversible Carbon Monoxide Insertion and Extrusion*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-66412-5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-66412-5).

title: Broad photochemical deracemization without molecular damage
open: Convert racemates to either chosen enantiomer across diverse stereogenic motifs while preserving other stereocenters and photolabile groups, with efficient photon use and practical temperatures.
status: Rapidly expanding since the 2010s. Copper-catalyzed photoderacemization in 2025 covered secondary and tertiary alkyl halides, including tetrasubstituted centers; general transferability remains open.
why: Converts an entire racemate into a selected enantiomer without simple resolution’s yield limitation.
key_works: Zhong et al. (2025), *Photoinduced copper-catalysed deracemization of alkyl halides*, [DOI:10.1038/s41586-025-08784-8](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-08784-8).

title: Efficient chemical motors under sustained useful loads
open: Engineer fully synthetic, chemically fueled motors delivering sustained work against external loads with quantified fuel-to-work efficiency, reliability and controllable speed.
status: Synthetic motors have developed for decades. Catalysis-driven polymer-gel contraction was demonstrated in 2025; efficient reusable operation under diverse prescribed loads remains open.
why: Turns molecular motion into useful actuation and transport.
key_works: Wang et al. (2025), *Transducing chemical energy through catalysis by an artificial molecular motor*, [DOI:10.1038/s41586-024-08288-x](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-08288-x).

title: Independent sequence and stereochemical programming of polymers
open: Independently specify stereogenic configurations along an already prescribed long-chain connectivity sequence, beyond repeating motifs or stereoregular blocks.
status: Longstanding. A 2025 ring-opening polymerization platform controlled stereochemistry and sequence sufficiently to produce selected AB and ABA materials; arbitrary joint programming remains open.
why: Separates composition, ordering and chirality effects on material properties.
key_works: Wang et al. (2025), *High-performance recyclable polymers enabled by stereo- and sequence-controlled polymerization*, [DOI:10.1038/s41557-025-01828-6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41557-025-01828-6).

title: Universal tacticity control in radical polymerization
open: Control tacticity across diverse vinyl monomers, including strongly polar substituents, without requiring special bulky pendant groups followed by their replacement.
status: A longstanding gap. Pan and Ouchi obtained approximately 99% meso-dyad polyacrylamides in 2025 using a transformable bulky pendant; general direct control remains open.
why: Combines practical radical processing with precision thermal and mechanical properties.
key_works: Pan and Ouchi (2025), *Post-polymerization modification enabling library synthesis of highly isotactic polyacrylamides carrying different pendant groups*, [DOI:10.1038/s42004-025-01663-3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42004-025-01663-3).

title: Polypropylene-to-propylene without large coproduct streams
open: Convert real polypropylene waste selectively into propylene at high carbon yield without large unwanted coproduct streams, excessive reagent co-feed or rapid deactivation.
status: Longstanding. Base-metal ethenolysis in 2024 converted polypropylene and mixed polyolefins to light olefins, including propylene/isobutylene mixtures; propylene-focused circularity remains open.
why: Recovers the original high-volume monomer from polypropylene products.
key_works: Conk et al. (2024), *Polyolefin waste to light olefins with ethylene and base-metal heterogeneous catalysts*, [DOI:10.1126/science.adq7316](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adq7316).

title: Closed-reagent-loop silicone recycling
open: Recycle diverse filled and cross-linked silicones while recovering silicone feedstocks and auxiliary reagents, controlling catalyst loss and impurity accumulation.
status: Gallium/BCl₃ chemistry in 2025 converted varied silicone wastes into key chlorosilanes near quantitatively at 40 °C. Closing auxiliary loops and demonstrating prolonged plant operation remain open.
why: Conserves embedded silicon-processing energy and valuable feedstocks.
key_works: Vu et al. (2025), *Gallium-catalyzed recycling of silicone waste with boron trichloride to yield key chlorosilanes*, [DOI:10.1126/science.adv0919](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adv0919).

title: Reactive oxidant in particulate methane monooxygenase
open: Identify the oxygen-derived species that cleaves methane’s C–H bond in active membrane-bound pMMO and establish its formation and decay kinetics.
status: Structural studies narrowed copper-site assignments. Calculations in 2024–2025 proposed distinguishable oxidant-generation mechanisms requiring decisive turnover experiments.
why: Supplies mechanistic guidance for selective methane oxidation.
key_works: Lundgren et al. (2025), *The CuB site in particulate methane monooxygenase may be used to produce hydrogen peroxide*, [DOI:10.1039/D4DT03301A](https://doi.org/10.1039/D4DT03301A).

title: Coordinated protocell genome and membrane reproduction
open: Build chemically simple compartments whose genome copying, membrane growth, division and inheritance remain coordinated across many generations without protein machinery.
status: Components have decades of demonstrations. Mixed-sequence RNA copying inside fatty-acid vesicles was shown in 2018; integrated hereditary reproduction remains open.
why: Defines a constructive intermediate between chemistry and cells.
key_works: O’Flaherty et al. (2018), *Copying of Mixed-Sequence RNA Templates inside Model Protocells*, [DOI:10.1021/jacs.8b00639](https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.8b00639).

title: Protocell nutrient entry without genome leakage
open: Obtain membranes admitting replication feedstocks while retaining genetic polymers and remaining stable under the ions and environmental cycles required by copying.
status: The permeability–retention conflict is longstanding. Vesicle experiments in 2018 admitted short oligonucleotides; compatibility across repeated reproduction cycles remains unresolved.
why: Prevents replicating compartments from starving or losing hereditary information.
key_works: O’Flaherty et al. (2018), *Copying of Mixed-Sequence RNA Templates inside Model Protocells*, [DOI:10.1021/jacs.8b00639](https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.8b00639).

title: Self-replenishing prebiotic nucleotide activation
open: Sustain nucleotide activation and reactivation in a copying-compatible network using plausible environmental energy, with explicit accounting for inhibitory by-products.
status: Activation chemistry is decades old. Photochemical activation and recycling were demonstrated in 2018; integration into sustained genome replication remains open.
why: Supplies the chemical free energy consumed by copying.
key_works: Mariani et al. (2018), *A Light-Releasable Potentially Prebiotic Nucleotide Activating Agent*, [DOI:10.1021/jacs.8b05189](https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.8b05189).

title: Parasite-resistant prebiotic replicator communities
open: Demonstrate chemically simple replicator populations that resist faster parasitic sequences while preserving innovation and cooperation under plausible compartment cycles.
status: Transient compartmentalization suppressed parasite takeover experimentally in 2016. Comparable robustness with wholly prebiotic replication chemistry remains open.
why: Addresses an evolutionary failure mode beyond successful copying.
key_works: Matsumura et al. (2016), *Transient compartmentalization of RNA replicators prevents extinction due to parasites*, [PubMed record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27940874/).

title: Why D-RNA became coupled to L-proteins
open: Identify and discriminate mechanisms establishing the observed relationship between sugar and amino-acid handedness, including historical contingency and chemical bias.
status: A longstanding specificity question. Tests of 15 self-aminoacylating ribozymes in 2024 found both chiral preferences, challenging a universal D-RNA-to-L-amino-acid bias.
why: Explains the particular handedness pairing beyond homochirality itself.
key_works: Kenchel et al. (2024), *Prebiotic chiral transfer from self-aminoacylating ribozymes may favor either handedness*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-024-52362-x](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-52362-x).

title: Representative certified nanoplastic reference materials
open: Produce traceable references spanning weathered polymers, irregular shapes, additive mixtures, sizes and environmental matrices, with independently certified properties.
status: Reference materials already exist. Work published online in 2025 introduced laser-generated model particles and discussed NPPP-1; representative coverage and cross-method certification remain incomplete.
why: Enables reproducible recovery estimates, method comparison and dose–response experiments.
key_works: Pegoraro et al. (2026; online 2025), *Nanoplastic reference materials for biological and methodological assessment*, [DOI:10.1186/s43591-025-00157-2](https://doi.org/10.1186/s43591-025-00157-2).

title: Closing organofluorine mass balances in complex products
open: Reconcile total, extractable, inorganic, polymeric and individually identified fluorine in realistic products and environmental samples within validated uncertainties.
status: Targeted PFAS assays leave unidentified fractions. A 2018 cosmetics study demonstrated substantial mass-balance gaps; general analytical closure remains open.
why: Prevents targeted testing from overlooking major fluorinated reservoirs.
key_works: Schultes et al. (2018), *Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances and fluorine mass balance in cosmetic products from the Swedish market: implications for environmental emissions and human exposure*, [DOI:10.1039/C8EM00368H](https://doi.org/10.1039/C8EM00368H).

title: Tire antiozonants without hazardous transformation products
open: Replace 6PPD with chemistry preserving tire durability and road safety while avoiding comparably hazardous parent compounds, transformation products and emissions.
status: 6PPD-quinone toxicity was identified in 2020–2021. California’s alternatives-analysis process documents continuing evaluation rather than an established universal substitute.
why: Reduces aquatic harm while maintaining tire performance.
key_works: Tian et al. (2021), *A ubiquitous tire rubber-derived chemical induces acute mortality in coho salmon*, [DOI:10.1126/science.abd6951](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.abd6951); California DTSC, [*Motor Vehicle Tires Containing 6PPD*](https://dtsc.ca.gov/scp/motor_vehicle_tires_containing_6ppd/).

title: Predicting oil-paint and acrylic-ground interfacial failure
open: Predict when pigment–binder–ground combinations develop cracks, protrusions or delamination from measured chemistry and environmental history.
status: Many degradation reactions are known. Interface-resolved analyses in 2025 linked early damage to chemical changes; a generally predictive lifetime model remains open.
why: Supports preventive conservation before irreversible visible damage.
key_works: Gnemmi et al. (2025), *Early degradation mechanisms at the interface between acrylic grounds and oil paint films*, [DOI:10.1038/s40494-025-01861-1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s40494-025-01861-1).

title: Optimal Lieb–Oxford constant
open: Determine the smallest universal constant bounding the indirect Coulomb energy by the integral of the electron density to the four-thirds power. Distinguish the unrestricted bound from exchange-only bounds and bounds for restricted physical states.
status: Open since the 1981 inequality. Lewin, Lieb and Seiringer’s 2022 proof gives an upper bound of approximately 1.58; the reported lower bound exceeds 1.44.
why: A sharper exact constraint would improve the mathematical foundation of exchange–correlation approximations.
key_works: M. Lewin, E. H. Lieb and R. Seiringer (2022), *Improved Lieb–Oxford bound on the indirect and exchange energies*, [arXiv:2203.12473](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.12473), DOI: 10.1007/s11005-022-01584-5.

title: Practical density functional satisfying the full flat-plane condition
open: Build an affordable functional that simultaneously respects piecewise linearity in electron number and constancy for fractional spin while giving reliable energies, densities and forces across bond breaking. Avoid case-specific corrections and artificial symmetry breaking.
status: Fractional-charge and fractional-spin failures were unified in 2008–2009. Fractional-spin corrections demonstrated successful molecular examples in 2018; a broadly transferable solution remains open.
why: One approximation could describe charge localization and static correlation consistently.
key_works: A. J. Cohen, P. Mori-Sánchez and W. Yang (2008), *Insights into current limitations of density functional theory*, [DOI:10.1126/science.1158722](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1158722); N. Q. Su, C. Li and W. Yang (2018), *Describing strong correlation with fractional-spin correction in density functional theory*, [article](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6166809/).

title: Predictive exchange–correlation steps in charge separation
open: Reproduce the spatial steps and derivative discontinuities that enforce correct electron allocation between weakly coupled fragments during dissociation and charge transfer. Predict their positions and heights from the system itself.
status: Recognized for decades. Analytical work in 2025 derived plateaus and investigated approximations; inexpensive general reproduction remains unresolved.
why: Incorrect fractional charge corrupts redox energetics and charge-transfer mechanisms.
key_works: N. E. Rahat and E. Kraisler (2025), *Plateaus in the Potentials of Density-Functional Theory: Analytical Derivation and Useful Approximations*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.jctc.4c01771](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jctc.4c01771); P. Mori-Sánchez and A. J. Cohen (2014), *The derivative discontinuity of the exchange-correlation functional*, [article](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24920317/).

title: Chemically useful tractable classes of the fermion sign problem
open: Characterize substantial, explicitly defined molecular Hamiltonian families for which unbiased quantum Monte Carlo avoids exponential sign degradation, or prove hardness within those families.
status: Troyer and Wiese established generic sign-problem NP-hardness in 2005. That result leaves the practical tractability boundary for structured molecular families incompletely characterized.
why: A classification would identify when unbiased correlation calculations can scale.
key_works: M. Troyer and U.-J. Wiese (2005), *Computational Complexity and Fundamental Limitations to Fermionic Quantum Monte Carlo Simulations*, [DOI:10.1103/PhysRevLett.94.170201](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.94.170201).

title: Robust transition-metal spin-state energetics
open: Predict spin-state free energies and equilibrium populations across oxidation states, temperatures and solvents with calibrated uncertainties.
status: Decades old. The 2024 SSE17 comparison found CCSD(T) best among the methods tested, with a mean absolute electronic-energy error of 1.5 kcal/mol.
why: Spin populations control magnetic properties and reaction pathways.
key_works: M. Radoń et al. (2024), *Performance of quantum chemistry methods for a benchmark set of spin-state energetics derived from experimental data of 17 transition metal complexes (SSE17)*, [DOI:10.1039/D4SC05471G](https://doi.org/10.1039/D4SC05471G).

title: Certified control of fixed-node bias
open: Obtain usable bounds on fixed-node energy errors for complex molecules, or a demonstrably convergent procedure reducing them to a prescribed tolerance.
status: Fixed-node diffusion Monte Carlo has been powerful for decades, but nodal bias remains difficult to certify. Neural trial wavefunctions improved molecular calculations in 2023; small sampling errors do not certify small nodal errors.
why: Certification would make numerical predictions quantitatively trustworthy.
key_works: W. Ren, W. Fu, X. Wu and J. Chen (2023), *Towards the ground state of molecules via diffusion Monte Carlo on neural networks*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-023-37609-3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-023-37609-3); [arXiv:2204.13903](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.13903).

title: Affordable coupled electron–nuclear quantum dynamics
open: Simulate chemically useful real-time motion with electrons and nuclei both treated quantum mechanically, controlling spatial discretization, pseudopotential and readout errors.
status: A 2025 proposal estimated 808 logical qubits and approximately \(10^{11}\) Toffoli gates per femtosecond for an ammonia–boron-trifluoride example. Affordable implementation remains a substantial gap.
why: It would address reactions where electronic transitions and nuclear tunneling are inseparable.
key_works: F. H. da Jornada et al. (2025), *A comprehensive framework to simulate real-time chemical dynamics on a fault-tolerant quantum computer*, [arXiv:2504.06348](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.06348), preprint.

title: Entanglement-assisted selection of bimolecular products
open: Experimentally control product-state branching by deliberately entangling reactants, and distinguish the advantage from ordinary reactant-state preparation.
status: A 2025 calculation predicted complete control of product rotational parity for an ultracold KRb + KRb example. Experimental implementation and generalization remain open.
why: Entanglement could become an independent resource for chemical selectivity.
key_works: A. Devolder, T. Tscherbul and P. Brumer (2025), *Leveraging Reactant Entanglement in the Coherent Control of Ultracold Bimolecular Chemical Reactions*, [DOI:10.1103/7c2n-xkpg](https://doi.org/10.1103/7c2n-xkpg); [arXiv:2505.10684](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.10684).

title: Isotope shifts of water’s liquid–liquid transition
open: Determine H₂O–D₂O shifts in liquid–liquid coexistence and critical parameters experimentally, and predict them with controlled electronic and nuclear quantum errors.
status: Path-integral calculations, including a 2026 equation-of-state study, quantify shifts within specific models. A model-independent experimental phase diagram for both isotopes remains absent.
why: Isotope effects can separate nuclear quantum contributions from classical network mechanisms.
key_works: A. Eltareb et al. (2026), *Nuclear Quantum Effects on the Equation of State of Water: Insights from the Potential Energy Landscape Formalism*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.jctc.5c02151](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jctc.5c02151).

title: Convention-consistent single-ion hydration energetics
open: Reconcile calculated and experimentally inferred single-ion hydration free energies under shared surface-potential and electrochemical conventions, with quantified electronic, finite-size and interfacial errors.
status: Debated for decades. Quantum simulations provide operationally defined scales, including the 2017 study below; broad transferable accuracy remains incomplete. A convention-free absolute single-ion number is not a physically appropriate target.
why: Ion energetics underpin acidity, solubility and electrochemical interfaces.
key_works: T. T. Duignan, M. D. Baer, G. K. Schenter and C. J. Mundy (2017), *Real single ion solvation free energies with quantum mechanical simulation*, [DOI:10.1039/C7SC02138K](https://doi.org/10.1039/C7SC02138K).

title: Surface dependence of anomalous electrolyte underscreening
open: Determine when long force-decay lengths in concentrated electrolytes reflect bulk screening, clustering or surface-specific effects. Predict concentration and substrate dependence consistently across measurement methods.
status: Positive and null observations coexist. A 2025 simulation connected long-ranged forces to solvent-induced clusters but did not reproduce the full concentration dependence.
why: Screening models determine predictions of colloidal stability and interfacial ion organization.
key_works: D. Ribar, C. E. Woodward and J. Forsman (2025), *Solvent-induced ion clusters generate long-ranged double-layer forces at high ionic strengths*, [DOI:10.1039/D5SM00027K](https://doi.org/10.1039/D5SM00027K).

title: Complete structure searches for flexible molecular crystals
open: Generate all experimentally relevant low-free-energy packings of flexible molecules, salts and coordination compounds, with meaningful search-completeness diagnostics.
status: The seventh blind test, reported in 2024, showed stronger performance for simple targets than complex systems; two groups first blindly predicted disorder.
why: Energy ranking cannot recover a relevant structure that was never generated.
key_works: L. M. Hunnisett et al. (2024), *The seventh blind test of crystal structure prediction: structure generation methods*, [DOI:10.1107/S2052520624007492](https://doi.org/10.1107/S2052520624007492).

title: Predicting cocrystal stoichiometry and competing phases
open: Predict cocrystal stoichiometries and competition with separate crystals, salts, solvates and disordered phases. Validate composition-dependent phase diagrams.
status: The 2024 seventh blind test explored stoichiometry prediction and found promising approaches; a generally reliable joint composition-and-structure predictor remains open.
why: Stoichiometry determines material properties and synthetic accessibility.
key_works: L. M. Hunnisett et al. (2024), *The seventh blind test of crystal structure prediction: structure generation methods*, [DOI:10.1107/S2052520624007492](https://doi.org/10.1107/S2052520624007492).

title: Reliable polymorph stability ranking at ambient conditions
open: Rank closely competing molecular-crystal free energies with errors below their separations, including thermal, quantum and disorder effects.
status: In the 2024 seventh blind test, dispersion-corrected periodic DFT often agreed with experiment, but thermal corrections helped only some targets and calculations remained costly.
why: Stability ordering determines solid-form conversion and shelf-life risks.
key_works: L. M. Hunnisett et al. (2024), *The seventh blind test of crystal structure prediction: structure ranking methods*, [DOI:10.1107/S2052520624008679](https://doi.org/10.1107/S2052520624008679).

title: Predicted missing stable polymorph of blind-test target XXXII
open: Produce and characterize the predicted lower-free-energy form of target XXXII, or establish why its predicted stability or accessibility fails.
status: Several 2024 blind-test methods placed observed forms over 4 kJ/mol above predicted minima. A 2025 study still identified the missing global minimum.
why: It is a concrete test of computational discovery of hidden solid forms.
key_works: L. M. Hunnisett et al. (2024), *The seventh blind test of crystal structure prediction: structure ranking methods*, [DOI:10.1107/S2052520624008679](https://doi.org/10.1107/S2052520624008679); J. van de Streek et al. (2025), *A Conceptual Framework for the Crystallizability of Organic Compounds*, [DOI:10.1021/jacs.5c08933](https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.5c08933).

title: Affordable anharmonic lattice free energies
open: Compute converged anharmonic free-energy differences for large libraries of flexible and disordered molecular polymorphs, including finite-size errors, at practical cost.
status: Normalizing-flow calculations gave accurate free energies for two modeled ice polymorphs in 2025. Diverse molecular crystals remain a broader transfer and scaling challenge.
why: Anharmonic entropy can reverse polymorph stability rankings.
key_works: E. Olehnovics et al. (2025), *Accurate Lattice Free Energies of Packing Polymorphs from Probabilistic Generative Models*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.jctc.4c01612](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jctc.4c01612).

title: Carrier of the 5780 Å diffuse interstellar band
open: Identify the carrier through laboratory spectra matching the astronomical wavelength, profile and companion transitions, with a plausible abundance.
status: Unidentified since Heger’s 1922 report. A 2025 quantum-chemical study rejected several proposed molecular families through incompatible spectra.
why: Identification would turn a widespread absorption feature into a chemical diagnostic.
key_works: H. Seuret et al. (2025), *Vetting molecular candidates posited for the first diffuse interstellar bands (5780 and 5797 Å): a quantum chemical study*, [DOI:10.1039/D4CP04023F](https://doi.org/10.1039/D4CP04023F).

title: Carrier of the 5797 Å diffuse interstellar band
open: Assign this band’s carrier and reproduce its spectrum and environmental dependence independently of the 5780 Å assignment.
status: Open since 1922. Correlated band families and candidate calculations constrain possibilities; a confirmed molecular assignment remains lacking.
why: It would identify a chemically informative component of interstellar matter.
key_works: H. Seuret et al. (2025), *Vetting molecular candidates posited for the first diffuse interstellar bands (5780 and 5797 Å): a quantum chemical study*, [DOI:10.1039/D4CP04023F](https://doi.org/10.1039/D4CP04023F).

title: Missing interstellar oxygen reservoir
open: Locate and quantify oxygen absent from observed gas, silicates and conventional ice inventories in translucent and dense clouds, closing the abundance budget with diagnostic spectra.
status: A longstanding depletion discrepancy persists. A 2025 analysis identifies far-infrared signatures of large icy grains as a discriminating observation.
why: Oxygen partition constrains planet-forming materials and water delivery.
key_works: T. Onaka, I. Sakon, T. Shimonishi and M. Honda (2025), *Searching for missing interstellar oxygen in the far-infrared*, [arXiv:2509.01846](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.01846).

title: Cold-cloud formation or survival of pyrene
open: Determine whether pyrene in TMC-1 forms locally at low temperature or survives transport from warmer regions, reproducing abundances and nitrile-isomer ratios with constrained kinetics.
status: Cyanopyrene detections in 2024–2025 established four-ring aromatic chemistry in a cold cloud. The parent aromatic inventory’s origin remains unresolved.
why: It tests how large carbon molecules arise before star formation.
key_works: G. Wenzel et al. (2024), *Detection of interstellar 1-cyanopyrene: A four-ring polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon*, [DOI:10.1126/science.adq6391](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adq6391); G. Wenzel et al. (2025), *Detections of interstellar aromatic nitriles 2-cyanopyrene and 4-cyanopyrene in TMC-1*, [DOI:10.1038/s41550-024-02410-9](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41550-024-02410-9).

title: Interstellar enantiomeric excess
open: Measure a nonzero enantiomeric excess, or a useful upper bound, for an interstellar chiral molecule using handedness-sensitive observations with controlled polarization errors.
status: Propylene oxide was detected in 2016, establishing identity without measuring handedness. Meteorite measurements concern different samples and histories.
why: It would constrain astronomical contributions to biological handedness.

title: Synthesis and identification of element 119
open: Produce nuclei with atomic number 119 and establish their identity through reproducible decay or mass evidence.
status: Still a search target in the 2026 experimental review. A 2022 barrier measurement constrained reaction energies for ⁵¹V + ²⁴⁸Cm without establishing synthesis.
why: It would open the eighth period and test nuclear stability and relativistic periodicity.

(2022), *Probing Optimal Reaction Energy for Synthesis of Element 119 from 51V+248Cm Reaction with Quasielastic Barrier Distribution Measurement*, [DOI:10.7566/JPSJ.91.084201](https://doi.org/10.7566/JPSJ.91.084201); J. M. Gates and J. L. Pore (2026), *The Quest for Superheavy Nuclei: An Experimental Perspective*, [DOI:10.1146/annurev-nucl-100324-103404](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-nucl-100324-103404).

title: Synthesis and identification of element 120
open: Produce and identify element 120 with decay assignments and reaction evidence sufficient for independent confirmation.
status: Searches remain underway in the 2026 review. Livermorium production using a ⁵⁰Ti beam in 2024 demonstrated precursor technology.
why: It tests shell stabilization and extends experimentally known periodicity.

(2024), *Toward the Discovery of New Elements: Production of Livermorium (Z=116) with 50Ti*, [DOI:10.1103/PhysRevLett.133.172502](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.133.172502); J. M. Gates and J. L. Pore (2026), *The Quest for Superheavy Nuclei: An Experimental Perspective*, [DOI:10.1146/annurev-nucl-100324-103404](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-nucl-100324-103404).

title: Experimental chemical properties of oganesson
open: Measure an oganesson chemical or response property, such as adsorption, polarizability or molecular binding, to test relativistic predictions.
status: Individual nuclei exist, while chemical behavior remains computationally inferred. A 2020 calculation predicted major departures from lighter noble gases; atom scarcity and short lifetimes obstruct experiments.
why: Oganesson is an extreme test of the basis of periodic trends.
key_works: O. R. Smits et al. (2020), *Oganesson: A Noble Gas Element That Is Neither Noble Nor a Gas*, [DOI:10.1002/anie.202011976](https://doi.org/10.1002/anie.202011976).

title: Defect-controlled thorium isomer quenching
open: Engineer host defects allowing efficient, switchable nuclear-state readout or reset while preserving coherence and frequency stability during interrogation.
status: Photoinduced quenching was demonstrated in 2025. Defect-mediated internal conversion explains observations, but reproducible materials design with quantified clock tradeoffs remains open.
why: Controlled reset could shorten measurement cycles and improve detection.
key_works: J. E. S. Terhune et al. (2025), *Photoinduced quenching of the 229Th isomer in a solid-state host*, [DOI:10.1103/glzr-thyw](https://doi.org/10.1103/glzr-thyw).

title: Productive direct aqueous dinitrogen electroreduction
open: Demonstrate reproducible net conversion of purified N₂ to ammonia in water at useful rates and selectivity, with isotope tracing, complete nitrogen balances and independent replication.
status: Pursued for decades; contamination remains decisive. Schneider et al. found in 2025 that reported Fe/Zn–N–C activity disappeared when nitrogen-oxide contamination was excluded.
why: It could simplify ammonia electrosynthesis by eliminating reactive-metal mediation.
key_works: C. Schneider et al. (2025), *Reevaluating the Activity of ZIF-8 Based FeNCs for Electrochemical Ammonia Production*, [primary institutional record](https://www.materials.ox.ac.uk/publication/2352947/ora-hyrax).

title: Sacrificial-reagent-free molecular photofixation of nitrogen
open: Couple molecular nitrogen reduction to water oxidation so light, nitrogen and water are the only net inputs and ammonia and oxygen the net products.
status: Molecular fixation has advanced since the early 2000s. Yamazaki et al. achieved visible-light ammonia formation with water in 2025, while tertiary phosphines supplied sacrificial reducing equivalents.
why: It would establish a materially closed artificial photosynthetic ammonia cycle.
key_works: Y. Yamazaki, Y. Endo and Y. Nishibayashi (2025), *Catalytic ammonia formation from dinitrogen, water, and visible light energy*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-59727-w](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59727-w).

title: Coke-resistant nonoxidative methane aromatization
open: Sustain methane-to-aromatics conversion while preventing persistent coke formation and avoiding frequent regeneration that damages the catalyst.
status: A decades-old challenge. A 2024 Pt–Bi/Mo/ZSM-5 study reported 18.7% methane conversion and 69.4% benzene selectivity; lifetime and joint performance remain limiting.
why: It would co-produce aromatic feedstocks and hydrogen directly from methane.
key_works: W. Bian et al. (2024), *Direct conversion of methane to aromatics and hydrogen via a heterogeneous trimetallic synergistic catalyst*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-024-47595-9](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-47595-9).

title: Multicarbon electrolysis of variable impure CO₂ feeds
open: Maintain controlled output as dilute CO₂ feeds vary in oxygen, sulfur and nitrogen impurities, with measured poisoning, regeneration and carbon balances.
status: Fang et al. tested dilute feeds and selected flue-gas impurities in 2026. Long-life operation under realistic mixed-impurity histories remains open.
why: It could reduce the upstream purification burden.
key_works: M. Fang et al. (2026), *Thousand-hour salt precipitation-free CO2-to-ethylene electrosynthesis at high current densities*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-67719-z](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-67719-z).

title: Practical iridium-free acidic oxygen evolution
subfield: Water splitting, hydrogen production and fuel cells
open: Demonstrate an acidic oxygen-evolution catalyst combining useful current density, low voltage and long membrane-electrode-assembly lifetime, with a complete dissolution balance.
status: Long sought. A 2025 cobalt study separated catalysis, corrosion and regeneration; self-reformation alone does not establish negligible material loss.
why: It could remove a critical-material bottleneck in PEM hydrogen production.
key_works: D. Simondson et al. (2025), *Decoupling the catalytic and degradation mechanisms of cobalt active sites during acidic water oxidation*, [DOI:10.1038/s41560-025-01812-x](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41560-025-01812-x).

title: Material-based hydrogen storage meeting complete system targets
open: Meet DOE ultimate usable system capacities of 6.5 wt% hydrogen and 50 g/L simultaneously with delivery, refueling, cost and lifetime requirements.
status: A decades-old target. Screening nearly half a million MOFs produced high-performing materials in 2019; complete systems must also account for vessels, cooling and unusable residual hydrogen.
why: It would support compact hydrogen transport with competitive system mass and volume.
key_works: U.S. DOE, *DOE Technical Targets for Onboard Hydrogen Storage for Light-Duty Vehicles*, [official table, accessed 2026-10-06](https://www.energy.gov/cmei/fuels/doe-technical-targets-onboard-hydrogen-storage-light-duty-vehicles); A. Ahmed et al. (2019), *Exceptional hydrogen storage achieved by screening nearly half a million metal-organic frameworks*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-019-09365-w](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-019-09365-w).

title: Uniform maximum atomic excess charge
open: Prove that a nucleus of charge \(Z\) can bind at most \(Z+C\) electrons, with \(C\) independent of \(Z\), for the full nonrelativistic many-electron Coulomb Hamiltonian.
status: The Hartree–Fock analogue is established, while the interacting Schrödinger problem remains open. A 2025 result gives the explicit bound \(N_c<1.1185Z+4Z^{1/3}\) for \(Z\ge4\), which still permits an excess increasing with nuclear charge.

title: All-weight extension of atomic ionization bounds
open: Prove \(N_c(Z)<b(s)Z+c(s)Z^{1/3}\) for every \(s\ge1\), where \(b(s)=\max_{0\le t\le1}(1+t^{s-1})/(1+t^s)\) and \(c(s)\) is finite. The unresolved range is \(s>3\), including quantitative control of \(c(s)\).
status: Hundertmark, Pattakos and Schulz proved the weighted estimate for \(1<s\le3\) and explicitly conjectured its extension in 2025.
why: Since \(b(s)\to1\), the extension could substantially strengthen finite-atom ionization bounds.
key_works: Hundertmark, Pattakos and Schulz (2025), *On the Excess Charge Problem of Atoms*, Remark 2.3, [arXiv:2504.18487](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.18487).

title: Uniform first-ionization-energy bound
open: Prove that \(E_Z(Z-1)-E_Z(Z)\le C\) for neutral atoms, uniformly in nuclear charge, with the complete electron–electron interaction.
status: A longstanding component of the ionization conjecture. Solovej proved the Hartree–Fock version; the full Schrödinger problem remains open because available total-energy asymptotics do not control the required order-one difference.
why: Places the bounded energy scale of outer-electron chemistry on a many-body foundation.
key_works: J. P. Solovej (2003), *The Ionization Conjecture in Hartree-Fock Theory*, [arXiv:math-ph/0012026](https://arxiv.org/abs/math-ph/0012026); M. Lewin (2025), *Some open mathematical problems concerning charged quantum particles*, [DOI:10.5802/crphys.249](https://doi.org/10.5802/crphys.249).

title: Uniform outer-electron radius bound
open: Define \(R_m(Z)\) so that a fixed number \(m>0\) of electrons lie outside that radius in a neutral atom. Establish \(Z\)-independent bounds, with the appropriate dependence on \(m\), for the full interacting theory.
status: Corresponding Hartree–Fock ionization-radius results are proved. Comparable exact many-electron density-tail control remains a decades-old problem.
why: Explains why chemically relevant valence length scales need not shrink with the atomic core.
key_works: J. P. Solovej (2003), *The Ionization Conjecture in Hartree-Fock Theory*, [arXiv:math-ph/0012026](https://arxiv.org/abs/math-ph/0012026).

title: Sharp three-dimensional Lieb–Thirring kinetic constant
open: Determine the optimal three-dimensional fermionic kinetic-energy constant, equivalently the sharp Lieb–Thirring spectral constant at \(\gamma=1\). Resolve whether the semiclassical value is optimal.
status: Open since the 1970s. The semiclassical constant was proved for shifted Coulomb Hamiltonians in 2025; arbitrary admissible potentials remain unresolved.
why: Sharpens electronic kinetic-energy lower bounds and quantitative stability estimates for matter.
key_works: T. C. Corso and T. Ried (2025), *On a Variational Problem Related to the Cwikel–Lieb–Rozenblum and Lieb–Thirring Inequalities*, [DOI:10.1007/s00220-024-05216-y](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00220-024-05216-y); Corso, T. Weidl and Z. Zeng (2025), *Lieb–Thirring inequalities for the shifted Coulomb Hamiltonian*, [DOI:10.4171/JST/574](https://doi.org/10.4171/JST/574).

title: Hohenberg–Kohn mapping for the physical total current
open: Determine whether particle density and physical total current uniquely determine scalar and vector potentials, modulo gauge, under precise ground-state assumptions. Alternatively, construct a counterexample identifying the missing information.
status: Standard paramagnetic-current uniqueness fails, and proposed total-current arguments have known defects. The physical-current mapping remains unresolved after the 2021 analysis of Diener’s construction.
why: Supports reliable density-functional descriptions of magnetic response and molecular currents.
key_works: A. Laestadius, M. Penz and E. I. Tellgren (2021), *Revisiting density-functional theory of the total current density*, [DOI:10.1088/1361-648X/abf784](https://doi.org/10.1088/1361-648X/abf784).

title: Generic coupled-cluster singles-and-doubles root counts
open: Derive a usable formula for the generic number of isolated complex CCSD amplitude solutions as electron and orbital counts vary, distinguishing arbitrary algebraic systems from physical two-body Hamiltonians.
status: Algebraic geometry provides bounds and special cases. The Grassmannian CCS degree is solved; arbitrary-size CCSD root counts are not.
why: Quantifies solution multiplicity and the completeness requirements of continuation algorithms.
key_works: F. M. Faulstich, B. Sturmfels and S. Sverrisdóttir (2025), *Algebraic Varieties in Quantum Chemistry*, [DOI:10.1007/s10208-024-09657-8](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10208-024-09657-8).

title: Computable coupled-cluster truncation error certificates
open: Produce rigorous, evaluable error bars for practical truncated coupled-cluster energies, with tests detecting failure of the assumptions behind the certificate.
status: Recent analysis proves local well-posedness and a posteriori estimates under structural assumptions. Inexpensively evaluating stability constants and missing-correlation bounds for difficult molecules remains open.
why: Distinguishes convergence of the amplitude solver from chemical accuracy.
key_works: M. Hassan, Y. Maday and Y. Wang (2023), *Analysis of the Single Reference Coupled Cluster Method for Electronic Structure Calculations: The Discrete Coupled Cluster Equations*, [arXiv:2311.00637](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.00637).

title: Guaranteed numerical errors for nonconvex Kohn–Sham calculations
open: Give computable energy-error bounds for nonconvex Kohn–Sham functionals, accounting for discretization and self-consistency while distinguishing local stationary states from the global minimum.
status: Guaranteed bounds were obtained for periodic equations with convex density functionals in 2025. Many practical exchange-correlation approximations violate that central hypothesis.
why: Makes numerical phase orderings and energy differences testable independently of functional approximation error.
key_works: A. Bordignon et al. (2025), *Fully Guaranteed and Computable Error Bounds on the Energy for Periodic Kohn–Sham Equations with Convex Density Functionals*, [DOI:10.1137/25M1735676](https://doi.org/10.1137/25M1735676).

title: Selecting the physical branch of self-consistent Green’s functions
open: Establish criteria selecting the physical equilibrium solution among self-consistent GF2 or GW branches, while distinguishing genuine metastability from diagrammatic-truncation artifacts.
status: Multiple solutions are documented. Pokhilko and Zgid’s 2025 homotopy method tracks Dyson-equation branches, including NdNiO₂ examples, without resolving universal physical branch selection.
why: Prevents a converged numerical solution from receiving an unjustified thermodynamic interpretation.
key_works: P. Pokhilko and D. Zgid (2025), *Homotopy continuation method for solving Dyson equation fully self-consistently: Theory and application to NdNiO2*, [DOI:10.1063/5.0288359](https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0288359).

title: Quantitative microscopic prediction of chiral spin selectivity
open: Predict spin-polarization magnitude, sign and temperature dependence from molecular structure and contacts without fitting artificially large spin–orbit coupling.
status: Competing mechanisms reproduce subsets of CISS experiments. A 2025 ab initio Hubbard-model parametrization demonstrates consequential electron–vibration effects, but a transferable quantitative theory remains unresolved.
why: Enables rational design of chiral spin filters and spin-dependent reactions.
key_works: D. K. A. Phan Huu et al. (2025), *Ab initio parametrization of a generalized Hubbard model in a molecule displaying chirality-induced spin selectivity*, [DOI:10.1038/s43246-025-00821-3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43246-025-00821-3).

title: Separating molecular and contact contributions to CISS
open: Measure intrinsic molecular spin filtering and electrode-interface selectivity independently in the same device, with controls for current direction, magnetization, handedness and nonlinear voltage response.
status: Direction-dependent magnetic conductive AFM supplied evidence against a purely interfacial interpretation in one 2025 geometry. General decomposition across contacts and molecular families remains open.
why: Identifies which chemical modifications affect spin transport and which affect injection.
key_works: J. A. Albro et al. (2025), *Measurement Platform to Probe the Mechanism of Chiral-Induced Spin Selectivity through Direction-Dependent Magnetic Conductive Atomic Force Microscopy*, [DOI:10.1021/acsnano.5c04980](https://doi.org/10.1021/acsnano.5c04980).

title: Bright, stable emitters with inverted singlet–triplet gaps
open: Realize inverted-gap molecules combining appreciable oscillator strength, rapid triplet harvesting and operational device stability, with experimentally verified excited-state ordering.
status: Inverted-gap examples exist. A 2026 search screened 118,081 aza-hydrocarbons and proposed 34 candidates with oscillator strengths at least 0.01; their combined predicted advantages require experimental realization.
why: Could reduce exciton residence times and OLED efficiency losses.
key_works: R. Mahaan and Z. Shuai (2026), *Cost-Effective Digital Discovery of Aza-Hydrocarbons via Isomerization for Inverted Singlet–Triplet Emitters*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.jpclett.6c01031](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jpclett.6c01031).

title: Directly resolving the charge-density oscillation of correlation-driven migration
open: Resolve coherent electronic-density oscillations after selective ionization while excluding nuclear motion and incoherent populations as explanations.
status: Correlation-driven adenine signatures were reported in 2021. A 2025 study still identified direct observation of the predicted quantum beating as elusive and proposed infrared preparation with X-ray probing.
why: Tests whether correlation moves chemically meaningful charge before nuclei respond.
key_works: E. P. Månsson et al. (2021), *Real-time observation of a correlation-driven sub 3 fs charge migration in ionised adenine*, [DOI:10.1038/s42004-021-00510-5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42004-021-00510-5); C. Guiot du Doignon et al. (2025), *Correlation-driven charge migration triggered by infrared multi-photon ionization*, [DOI:10.1039/D5SC02374B](https://doi.org/10.1039/D5SC02374B).

title: Direct observation of waveform-controlled Kolbe branching
open: Measure interfacial pH, radical populations and radical-to-carbocation conversion within individual polarity cycles, quantitatively explaining dimerization, substitution and overoxidation.
status: The 2023 waveform study proposed local-pH effects. Cycle-resolved intermediate and product balances remain the experimental test of that mechanism.
why: Makes waveform selection transferable across substrates and reactors.
key_works: Y. Hioki et al. (2023), *Overcoming the limitations of Kolbe coupling with waveform-controlled electrosynthesis*, [DOI:10.1126/science.adf4762](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adf4762).

title: Enantioselective capture of unbound electrogenerated carbocations
open: Trap directly electrogenerated, non-catalyst-bound tertiary carbocations with predictable enantioselectivity before rearrangement or solvent capture, without covalently attached chiral auxiliaries.
status: A 2024 method controls chiral α-imino carbocations using primary-amine catalysis. Freely diffusing tertiary carbocations present a distinct unresolved selectivity problem.
why: Enables asymmetric substitutions at crowded carbon centers from oxidizable feedstocks.
key_works: Q. Lin et al. (2024), *Enantioselective SN1-type reaction via electrochemically generated chiral α-Imino carbocation intermediate*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-024-50945-2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-50945-2).

title: C–B axial chirality that survives Lewis-base coordination
open: Design axially chiral boron Lewis acids retaining configuration through repeated donor association and dissociation without sacrificing Lewis acidity.
status: Doan et al. showed in 2025 that Lewis-base binding can accelerate triarylborane atropisomerization from decades to minutes. Stability of the free borane therefore leaves catalytic-cycle stability unresolved.
why: Makes C–B atropisomers persistent asymmetric Lewis-acid catalysts.
key_works: T.-H. Doan et al. (2025), *Atropisomerism in Triarylboranes: Lewis Base Assisted Rotation at C−B Stereogenic Axis in Asymmetrical Boron Lewis Acids*, [DOI:10.1002/ange.202421931](https://doi.org/10.1002/ange.202421931).

title: Direct asymmetric NH transfer to dialkyl sulfoxides
open: Convert racemic dialkyl sulfoxides directly into enantioenriched unprotected NH-sulfoximines through catalytic NH transfer and simultaneous racemization.
status: Fan et al.’s 2025 iron/photoredox resolution performs well for many aryl–alkyl sulfoxides. The tested dialkyl substrate gave 29% yield and racemic product.
why: Provides compact sulfur stereocenters without chiral starting materials.
key_works: F.-X. Fan, H. Xu, S.-X. Tang, Y. Dang and F. Wang (2025), *Iron-catalysed stereoselective NH transfer enables dynamic kinetic resolution of sulfoxides*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-56860-4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-56860-4).

title: The dark racemization pathway in iron-catalyzed sulfoxide imidation
open: Identify the nonphotochemical racemization pathway in the iron/aminating-reagent system, distinguishing electron transfer, sulfur substitution and iron–aminyl chemistry, including the base’s role.
status: Dark racemization requiring iron, ligand and aminating reagent was observed in 2025. The additional pathway and base contribution remained unresolved.
why: Could enable simpler dynamic resolutions and suppress stereochemical erosion.
key_works: F.-X. Fan et al. (2025), *Iron-catalysed stereoselective NH transfer enables dynamic kinetic resolution of sulfoxides*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-56860-4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-56860-4).

title: Quantitative stereochemical proteome maps for sulfonimidoyl fluorides
open: Measure matched sulfur-enantiomer pairs’ residue occupancy and reaction kinetics across native proteomes while separately quantifying hydrolysis and nonspecific binding.
status: Buffer-phase stereospecific transformations and chirality-dependent protein ligation were demonstrated in 2024–2025. Quantitative proteome-wide stereochemical reactivity maps remain open.
why: Connects sulfur configuration to selective covalent recognition.
key_works: H.-S. Huang et al. (2025), *Enantioselective Synthesis of Chiral Sulfonimidoyl Fluorides Facilitates Stereospecific SuFEx Click Chemistry*, [DOI:10.1002/anie.202415873](https://doi.org/10.1002/anie.202415873).

title: Long heparan-sulfate chains with independently programmed epimers and sulfates
open: Specify every uronate epimer and N-, 2-O-, 3-O- and 6-O-sulfation site in long chains, preserving the pattern through synthesis and purification.
status: A 2023 platform produced all 64 N-/2-O-/6-O-sulfation patterns on a fixed tetrasaccharide framework. Long-chain epimer and 3-O-sulfate programming remain outside that comprehensive library.
why: Enables causal tests of long-range sulfation domains.
key_works: L. Wang et al. (2023), *Efficient platform for synthesizing comprehensive heparan sulfate oligosaccharide libraries for decoding glycosaminoglycan–protein interactions*, [DOI:10.1038/s41557-023-01248-4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41557-023-01248-4).

title: Complete native heparan-sulfate chain sequencing
open: Recover an individual native chain’s ordered sugars, uronate epimers and sulfation sites, retaining fragment provenance across long domains and rare 3-O-sulfated motifs.
status: The 2020 SIMMS² method used 36 synthetic di- to decasaccharide standards and sequenced natural hexasaccharides. Complete native-chain reconstruction remains beyond that fragment-level result.
why: Makes the proposed heparan-sulfate sequence code directly readable.
key_works: R. L. Miller et al. (2020), *Shotgun ion mobility mass spectrometry sequencing of heparan sulfate saccharides*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-020-15284-y](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-15284-y).

title: Unbiased quantitative inventories of heparan-sulfate 3-O-sulfation
open: Quantify native 3-O-sulfated motifs with calibrated recovery across neighboring sulfate patterns and epimers, distinguishing rarity from poor release, enrichment or ionization.
status: Cationic-peptide enrichment followed by HILIC–cyclic-ion-mobility MS improved detection in 2025. Absolute motif abundances still require recovery and selectivity corrections.
why: Enables reliable comparisons of rare but functionally important sulfation.
key_works: E. Mernie et al. (2025), *Untangling Heparan Sulfate 3-O-Sulfation Using a Novel Offline Cationic-Peptide Affinity Enrichment, Followed by HILIC-cIM-MS*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.analchem.4c05019](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.analchem.4c05019).

title: Native sialic-acid O-acetyl maps before migration
open: Recover the original C7/C8/C9 O-acetyl distribution while separately quantifying migration during quenching, extraction, digestion and analysis.
status: Reversible pH-dependent migration was established in 2021; positional and linkage assignment by ion-mobility MS followed in 2023. Preservation of the original biological distribution remains a separate requirement.
why: Prevents analytical rearrangement from masquerading as biological regulation.
key_works: Y. Ji et al. (2021), *Reversible O-Acetyl Migration within the Sialic Acid Side Chain and Its Influence on Protein Recognition*, [DOI:10.1021/acschembio.0c00998](https://doi.org/10.1021/acschembio.0c00998); G. M. Vos et al. (2023), *Sialic acid O-acetylation patterns and glycosidic linkage type determination by ion mobility-mass spectrometry*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-023-42575-x](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-023-42575-x).

title: Complete enzymatic release of structurally diverse O-glycans
open: Release intact mucin-type O-glycans across all eight cores and common extensions from native proteins without removing informative terminal modifications.
status: The 2025 POGases broadened release to cores 1, 2 and 3 and selected sialylated structures. Native substrates remained harder than denatured ones; combined core coverage and accessibility remain unresolved.
why: Reduces structural bias introduced before instrumental analysis.
key_works: L. Zhou et al. (2025), *Dual functional POGases from bacteria encompassing broader O-glycanase and adhesin activities*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-57143-8](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-57143-8).

title: Are wybutosine derivatives yW-72 and yW-86 glycoRNA attachment sites?
open: Determine whether native yW-72 and yW-86 carry covalent N-glycans and establish their bond structures, excluding indirect release or co-enrichment.
status: Xie et al. established acp³U attachment in 2024. Their experiments also recovered carboxyl-containing yW derivatives, but equivalent direct linkage proof remains missing.
why: Tests whether RNA glycosylation uses multiple attachment chemistries.
key_works: Xie et al. (2024), *The modified RNA base acp3U is an attachment site for N-glycans in glycoRNA*, [DOI:10.1016/j.cell.2024.07.044](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2024.07.044).

title: The enzyme that amidates acp³U before RNA N-glycosylation
open: Identify and reconstitute the proposed conversion of acp³U’s carboxyl group into a glycosylation-competent carboxamide, or establish an alternative linkage-forming route.
status: The 2024 acp³U study explicitly proposes an unidentified amidating enzyme upstream of oligosaccharyltransferase. Known genetic and transport dependencies do not identify that activity.
why: Closes a missing chemical step in glycoRNA biosynthesis.
key_works: Xie et al. (2024), *The modified RNA base acp3U is an attachment site for N-glycans in glycoRNA*, [DOI:10.1016/j.cell.2024.07.044](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2024.07.044).

title: Preventing delayed Cr(VI) rebound after reductive remediation
open: Predict and prevent Cr(VI) regeneration as Cr–Fe hydroxides age toward goethite in the presence of manganese, oxygen and changing pH.
status: A 2025 study found approximately tenfold higher Cr(VI) release following mineral transformation under its conditions. Long-term control across residue compositions remains open.
why: Ensures reduced chromium residues remain immobilized during aging.
key_works: S. Xie et al. (2025), *Enhanced oxidation of Cr(III) with the mineral transformation of CrxFe1-x(OH)3 in the presence of Mn(II): overlooked process during the reoccurrence of Cr(VI) in reduced chromite ore processing residue*, [DOI:10.1016/j.envpol.2025.126327](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.envpol.2025.126327).

title: Decoupling cement dispersion from hydrate-nucleation retardation
open: Design dispersants lowering water demand without unwanted setting delays, predicting separate effects on dissolution, hydrate nucleation and portlandite precipitation near saturation.
status: Four polymers inhibited hydrate nucleation without measurable dissolution inhibition under tested undersaturation in 2025. Near-saturation and mixed-clinker behavior remain unresolved.
why: Preserves early strength while reducing mixing water.
key_works: A. Vohburger et al. (2025), *Influence of Polymeric Dispersants on the Dissolution Rate of Tricalcium Silicate and the Nucleation of Calcium-Silicate-Hydrate and Portlandite*, [DOI:10.1002/chem.202500207](https://doi.org/10.1002/chem.202500207).

title: Distinguishing dissolution-driven and rearrangement-driven cement creep
open: Separate stress-assisted dissolution/reprecipitation, hydrate sliding and continuing hydration contributions to creep, predicting their humidity and composition dependence.
status: The microscopic origin remains debated. A 2025 study found continued fly-ash reaction increasing creep and foil-like C-A-S-H in slag blends inhibiting it; quantitative mechanism separation remains open.
why: Links hydrate chemistry to long-term structural deformation.
key_works: J. Wang et al. (2025), *Does the hydration process of supplementary cementitious materials affect the aging creep of blended cement paste?*, [DOI:10.1016/j.cemconres.2025.107826](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cemconres.2025.107826).

title: Predicting steel passivity after alkali-activated binder carbonation
open: Predict steel depassivation from evolving pore solutions and hydrates during carbonation, chloride exposure and leaching.
status: A 2025 calcined-clay/slag study observed no corrosion after the carbonation front reached steel, consistent with retained high pH. Conventional front criteria therefore lack universal transferability.
why: Provides chemically valid durability criteria for alternative binders.
key_works: S. D. C. Gomes et al. (2025), *Shrinkage and carbonation of alkali-activated calcined clay-ground granulated blast furnace slag (GGBFS) concrete*, [DOI:10.1016/j.cemconres.2025.107899](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cemconres.2025.107899).

title: Pair-specific RO₂ accretion branching beyond small radicals
open: Measure absolute reaction constants and accretion yields for unlike multifunctional peroxy-radical pairs, testing whether self-reaction rules predict cross-reactions.
status: A 2025 small-β-hydroxy-RO₂ study measured accretion-channel constants spanning approximately \(4.7\times10^{-13}\) to \(8.0\times10^{-16}\) cm³ molecule⁻¹ s⁻¹. Complex atmospheric radicals remain inadequately covered.
why: Controls low-volatility product formation and particle growth.
key_works: S. E. Murphy et al. (2025), *Accretion product formation in the self- and cross-reactions of small β-hydroxy peroxy radicals*, [DOI:10.1039/D5EA00106D](https://doi.org/10.1039/D5EA00106D).

title: Surface accretion of RO₂ on freshly nucleated particles
open: Directly test peroxy-radical accretion at sulfuric-acid/base nanoparticle interfaces, measuring competition with desorption and gas-phase reaction.
status: A 2026 computational study identified rapid candidate pathways. Particle-size-resolved experimental confirmation and atmospheric-flux relevance remain missing.
why: Could explain organic growth immediately after particle nucleation.
key_works: G. Hasan, T. Kurtén, I. Neefjes and J. Elm (2026), *Can Accretion Products Be Formed at the Interface of Freshly Nucleated Particles?*, [DOI:10.1021/acsomega.5c13316](https://doi.org/10.1021/acsomega.5c13316).

title: Isomer-resolved organic-nitrate hydrolysis in concentrated aerosol
open: Measure individual monoterpene-nitrate hydrolysis and competing reactions in low-water-activity aerosol across acidity, ionic strength and organic matrices.
status: Seven synthesized standards studied in 2021 showed strongly structure-dependent minute-to-hour lifetimes, with some secondary nitrates resistant under neutral conditions. Actual aerosol matrices remain insufficiently characterized.
why: Determines whether aerosol nitrates recycle atmospheric nitrogen oxides.
key_works: Y. Wang et al. (2021), *Synthesis and Hydrolysis of Atmospherically Relevant Monoterpene-Derived Organic Nitrates*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.est.1c05310](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.est.1c05310).

title: Origin of unequal nitrate-aerosol yields from the two phellandrenes
open: Identify particle-phase pathways explaining α-/β-phellandrene nitrate-oxidation yield differences, closing carbon and nitrate balances with resolved products.
status: A 2025 chamber study found maximum aerosol yields near 35% and 60%, respectively, despite similarities in measured gas chemistry. The condensed-phase explanation remains incomplete.
why: Tests how terpene structure should enter regional aerosol models.
key_works: S. Harb et al. (2025), *Highly oxygenated molecules (HOMs) and secondary organic aerosol (SOA) formation from the oxidation of α- and β-phellandrenes by NO3 radicals*, [DOI:10.5194/acp-25-11003-2025](https://doi.org/10.5194/acp-25-11003-2025).

title: Reactive-solute control of aqueous HPMTF sulfur branching
open: Determine whether realistic cloud solutes alter hydroperoxymethyl thioformate reaction mechanisms and branching, with closed sulfur and carbon balances.
status: A 2024 experiment already found sulfate consistent with unit yield and carbonyl sulfide below 1.2%; 2025 field observations confirmed substantial cloud removal. Solute-dependent chemistry remains unresolved.
why: Connects marine DMS oxidation to sulfate and carbonyl-sulfide budgets.
key_works: C. M. Jernigan et al. (2024), *Sulfate and Carbonyl Sulfide Production in Aqueous Reactions of Hydroperoxymethyl Thioformate*, [DOI:10.1021/acsestair.3c00098](https://doi.org/10.1021/acsestair.3c00098); D. B. Kilgour et al. (2025), *Cloud processing of dimethyl sulfide (DMS) oxidation products limits sulfur dioxide (SO2) and carbonyl sulfide (OCS) production in the eastern North Atlantic marine boundary layer*, [DOI:10.5194/acp-25-1931-2025](https://doi.org/10.5194/acp-25-1931-2025).

title: Chemical origin of nitryl chloride emitted during automotive braking
open: Identify chloride sources and reaction sequences generating braking-associated ClNO₂, separating new tribochemistry from release of existing material.
status: HONO, ClNO₂ and N₂O₅ were detected during braking in 2025. Precursor inventories and a closed nitryl-chloride production mechanism remain unresolved.
why: Reveals reactive gas emissions omitted by particle-mass inventories.
key_works: M. E. Cooke et al. (2025), *Emissions of Nitrous Acid, Nitryl Chloride, and Dinitrogen Pentoxide Associated with Automotive Braking*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.est.4c13202](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.est.4c13202).

title: Identity of the mid-polarity Pacific iron-binding ligand group
open: Isolate unidentified mid-polarity iron-binding compounds from the Pacific GP15 transect and determine structures, affinities and degradation pathways.
status: A 2025 survey found unresolved putative siderophores in upper-mesopelagic tropical waters. Coelution prevented confident molecular-ion and formula assignments.
why: Converts a recurrent oceanographic signal into an interpretable transport mechanism.
key_works: J. Li, L. Babcock-Adams, M. R. McIlvin and D. J. Repeta (2025), *Distribution and Cycling of Siderophores in the Eastern North and Tropical Pacific Oceans*, [DOI:10.1029/2024GL113874](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024GL113874).

title: Identity of non-cobalamin cobalt-binding ligands in the surface ocean
open: Identify strong cobalt ligands not accounted for by measurable cobalamins, including oxidation states and biological sources.
status: A 2025 North Pacific study measured approximately 31–87 pM dissolved cobalt without detecting cobalamin-related compounds in the corresponding strong-ligand pool. Remaining ligand structures are unknown.
why: Explains stabilization and exchange of scarce marine cobalt.
key_works: J. Park et al. (2025), *Efficient cobalamin uptake and cycling contribute to the lack of cobalamins in the surface cobalt-binding ligand pool in the North Pacific*, [DOI:10.1002/lol2.70019](https://doi.org/10.1002/lol2.70019).

title: Mechanisms converting dimethylmercury into monomethylmercury at depth
open: Identify and measure dimethylmercury conversion pathways below strongly illuminated surface waters independently of concentration-profile fitting.
status: A 2024 upwelling study inferred net loss of \(2.0\pm1.1\%\) per day from field profiles and mass-budget modeling. Direct pathway-specific field rates remain unresolved.
why: Explains methylmercury production away from immediate primary formation sites.
key_works: H. M. Adams, X. Cui, C. H. Lamborg and A. T. Schartup (2024), *Dimethylmercury as a Source of Monomethylmercury in a Highly Productive Upwelling System*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.est.4c01112](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.est.4c01112).

title: Chemical evolution and self-limiting growth of ZDDP tribofilms
open: Predict coupled phosphate-chain chemistry, film growth and removal under changing stresses, identifying the chemical feedbacks limiting thickness.
status: A 2023 study separated shear-promoted growth from compression-induced inhibition. A complete growth–conversion–removal network for service contacts remains missing.
why: Maintains wear protection with lower additive consumption.
key_works: L. Fang et al. (2023), *What stress components drive mechanochemistry? A study of ZDDP tribofilm formation*, [DOI:10.1039/D2FD00123C](https://doi.org/10.1039/D2FD00123C).

title: Native structure of soluble methane monooxygenase intermediate Q
open: Establish Q’s Fe–O connectivity, protonation and Fe–Fe distance while reconciling vibrational, X-ray and magnetic spectra for the same intermediate population.
status: Debated for over 30 years. A 2021 QM/MM study favors an open core; complete experimental discrimination from diamond-core assignments remains unresolved.
why: Identifies how a biological diiron center activates methane.
key_works: C. E. Schulz et al. (2021), *Structure–Spectroscopy Correlations for Intermediate Q of Soluble Methane Monooxygenase: Insights from QM/MM Calculations*, [DOI:10.1021/jacs.1c01180](https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.1c01180).

title: Substrate coordination in catalytically active methyl-coenzyme M reductase
open: Determine methyl-SCoM coordination in active Ni(I) enzyme through C–S cleavage, discriminating nickel–sulfonate binding from sulfur-coordinated alternatives.
status: A 2021 study supports nickel–sulfonate binding; 2025 atomic structures add constraints. A native active-state substrate-to-radical trajectory remains missing.
why: Establishes the geometry enabling methane formation and its reversal.
key_works: A. Patwardhan et al. (2021), *Nickel–Sulfonate Mode of Substrate Binding for Forward and Reverse Reactions of Methyl-SCoM Reductase Suggest a Radical Mechanism Involving Long-Range Electron Transfer*, [DOI:10.1021/jacs.1c01086](https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.1c01086); M.-C. Müller et al. (2025), [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-63387-1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-63387-1).

title: Functions of the unusual modifications in methane-oxidizing MCR
open: Assign individual post-translational modifications’ causal effects on methane activation, cofactor stability and directionality through controlled modification states and kinetics.
status: Atomic-resolution ANME-2c/2d structures identified extensive modifications in 2025. Their individual chemical functions remain unassigned.
why: Identifies maturation functions required when transferring methane-oxidation machinery.
key_works: M.-C. Müller et al. (2025), *Atomic resolution structures of the methane-activating enzyme in anaerobic methanotrophy reveal extensive post-translational modifications*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-63387-1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-63387-1).

title: Electron accounting during ACS thioester release
open: Determine whether native acetyl-CoA release uses oxidation-triggered nickel chemistry, tracking the transferred electron through enzyme reset.
status: One-electron oxidation accelerated thioester elimination approximately 1,800-fold in a 2025 model. The corresponding native oxidation sequence remains unverified.
why: Discriminates mechanisms with different electron-donor and cofactor requirements.
key_works: S. Nath, L. Griego and L. M. Mirica (2025), *The mechanism of acetyl-CoA synthase through the lens of a nickel model system*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-60163-z](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-60163-z).

title: Carrier of the 6614 Å diffuse interstellar band
open: Identify a molecule reproducing the band’s laboratory wavelength, substructure and environmental profile changes, with viable interstellar formation and survival.
status: Unassigned. A 2025 oblate-top fit suggests roughly 54 carbon atoms under that model; competing geometric interpretations remain possible.
why: Identifies a major molecular population hidden from rotational surveys.
key_works: C. Bhatt et al. (2025), *The EDIBLES Survey IX: Simulations of the λ6614 DIB Profile Variations: A Surprising Connection with CH⁺*, [DOI:10.1021/acsearthspacechem.4c00238](https://doi.org/10.1021/acsearthspacechem.4c00238); H. MacIsaac et al. (2022), [DOI:10.1051/0004-6361/202142225](https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202142225).

title: Carrier of the 6379 Å diffuse interstellar band
open: Identify the absorber while explaining rotational substructure and excitation changes, breaking the degeneracy between linear and approximately spherical geometries.
status: A 2022 contour analysis yields geometry-dependent rotational constants; the spherical interpretation implies roughly 77–114 carbons. No molecular formula is securely assigned.
why: Distinguishes chemical families with similar astronomical band profiles.
key_works: H. MacIsaac et al. (2022), *The EDIBLES survey V: Line profile variations in the λλ5797, 6379, and 6614 diffuse interstellar bands as a tool to constrain carrier sizes*, [DOI:10.1051/0004-6361/202142225](https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202142225); [arXiv:2203.01803](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.01803).

title: First identified optical transitions of neutral lawrencium
open: Observe and assign a neutral-lawrencium optical transition, then use the level structure to test predicted relativistic valence configurations.
status: The 2026 search scanned approximately 800 cm⁻¹ around each of two predicted strong transitions without detecting either. The experiment demonstrated efficient evaporation and sufficient sensitivity, leaving the transition locations or excitation assumptions unresolved.
why: Supplies direct electronic-level evidence for the final actinide.
key_works: E. Rickert et al. (2026), “Progress toward identifying atomic transitions in lawrencium,” [DOI: 10.1140/epjd/s10053-026-01198-9](https://doi.org/10.1140/epjd/s10053-026-01198-9).

title: Radium-223 chelation that survives tracer-level dilution in serum
open: Produce a molecular Ra(II) chelate that remains intact after dilution into serum, distinguishing intact complex from free radium in every analytical fraction. Demonstrate stability over the intended delivery interval without excess free ligand recapturing dissociated radium.
status: A 2026 screen achieved quantitative room-temperature labeling with 14 of 17 chelators, but even macropa dissociated within one hour at higher dilution. Apparently favorable size-exclusion results could conceal free radium.
why: Enables targeted radium delivery beyond its natural bone-seeking behavior.
key_works: J. W. Southwell, M. Gumiela et al. (2026), “Synthesis, Characterization, and Evaluation of Chelators for Radium-223,” [DOI: 10.1021/acs.inorgchem.5c04877](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.inorgchem.5c04877).

title: Does a transient cyclic astatinane protect ortho-substituted aryl–At bonds?
open: Detect or exclude the proposed intramolecular arylalkoxyastatinane formed when a neighboring benzyl-alcohol group encounters oxidized aryl astatine. Quantify its contribution to suppressed C–At cleavage.
status: Ortho alcohols improved resistance to chemical and microsomal oxidation in 2025. The hypothesized cyclic intermediate could not be observed, and steric shielding alone did not explain the chemical-oxidation results.
why: Turns an effective stabilization motif into a transferable radiolabel-design mechanism.
key_works: R. Fouinneteau, C. Maingueneau, N. Galland, C. Perrio, and F. Guérard (2025), “Ortho-functionalization of a 211At-labeled aryl compound provides stabilization of the C-At bond against oxidative dehalogenation,” [DOI: 10.1038/s41598-025-01162-4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-025-01162-4).

title: Unidentified cleavage products of lead–TCMC thiourea bioconjugates
open: Identify the radioactive metabolites and serum components that detach targeting vectors from Pb–TCMC thiourea conjugates. Distinguish linker cleavage from radiometal loss.
status: A 2025/2026 study found similar degradation products for FAPI and CycMSH conjugates; amide replacements improved stability. Attempts to identify products using nonradioactive lead and LC–MS encountered sensitivity limits, leaving their identities and formation mechanisms unresolved.
why: Prevents intact metal chelation from being mistaken for an intact targeting molecule.
key_works: B. L. McNeil et al. (2026; online 2025), “Is Thiourea the Weak Link? An Investigation of the In Vitro and In Vivo Destabilization of [203Pb]- and [212Pb]Pb2+ Thiourea-Based Bioconjugates,” [DOI: 10.1021/acsbiomedchemau.5c00224](https://doi.org/10.1021/acsbiomedchemau.5c00224).

title: Competitive-ligand boundary for loss of protactinium’s mono-oxo bond
